clue.text: Pays out to accept delivery of pack of nightwear

indicators.note: to accept delivery of something is to take it in, so the scrambled letters close round the next piece
out signals that the letters of the word pays are knocked out of their order

parts.note: to pack a space is to jam it

explanation.surface: Someone pays out to take in a package of sleepwear ordered by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PAYS to PYAS, and 'to accept delivery of' puts JAM inside it: PY-JAM-AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas are the loose jacket and trousers worn in bed, a standard item of sleepwear.

clue.text: Chapters about right idioms

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: chapters in a life or history are its phases or stages

explanation.surface: A grammar book's chapters deal with correct idioms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside PHASES.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set expression, a fixed form of words.

clue.text: One with knavish lack of mastery

definitions.text: One with knavish lack of mastery

parts.words: One with knavish lack of mastery
parts.note: a knave is the jack in a pack of cards, and the proverb about someone with many skills ends 'master of none', so the lack of mastery belongs to a versatile dabbler

explanation.walkthrough: 'knavish' points to the jack (the knave in a pack of cards), and 'lack of mastery' to the proverb's ending, 'master of none'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a person who can turn a hand to many skills but is expert in none.

clue.text: In grammar equine animal like this must be feminine

definitions.text: animal like this must be feminine

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning their join

explanation.surface: A grammar point: the word for this horse must take the feminine gender.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'grammAR Equine'. A female horse is necessarily feminine.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare is a female horse, so the creature is by nature female.

clue.text: Mischievous after short time being egotistic

indicators.note: after places the mischievous piece behind the short time in the answer

parts.note: S is short for second, a brief time
elfish means impish or mischievous, like an elf

explanation.surface: Someone is naughty for a moment, being self-centred.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotistic and selfish both describe putting oneself first without regard for others.

clue.text: Tents in front of house will need right kind of insect repellant

indicators.note: in front of says the tent piece comes before the house piece in the word

parts.note: a camp is a set of tents pitched together

explanation.surface: Campers in tents near a house will want something to keep the bugs off.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor is the strong-smelling compound in mothballs, used to keep moths and other insects away.

clue.text: Australian friend holds line for shoe repairer

indicators.note: holds means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate or friend

explanation.surface: An Aussie mate keeps a line for the cobbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts L inside COBBER, the Australian word for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler is a tradesman who mends shoes.

clue.text: Drink given me one day

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone is handed a drink one day.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink made by fermenting honey with water.

clue.text: One expecting to be displaced if better placed one is expecting!

definitions.text: One expecting to be displaced if better placed one is expecting!

parts.words: One expecting to be displaced if better placed one is expecting!
parts.note: a successor in line who would lose that place if a closer relative were born, the second 'expecting' meaning pregnant

explanation.walkthrough: The first 'expecting' means hoping to inherit, the second means pregnant: a birth to someone closer in line would push this successor down.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a next-in-line to a title or throne whose claim could be overtaken by the birth of a nearer heir.

clue.text: Particular bet accepted by soak

indicators.note: accepted by means the bet goes inside the soak word

parts.note: to ret flax or hemp is to soak it to soften the fibres
a spec is a speculation, a gamble or bet

explanation.surface: A drunk takes a particular wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' looks like a drunkard but is the verb RET; 'accepted by' puts SPEC inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a detail or point, as in 'in every respect'.

clue.text: Audio resources to log overlapping Zodiac constellations

parts.note: to log something is to record it

indicators.note: overlapping means the two star names share a letter where one ends and the other begins, so one copy goes

parts.note: Libra, the scales, is a constellation of the zodiac
Aries, the ram, is another constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An astronomer logs the zodiac constellations, perhaps as sound recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: LIBRA ends and ARIES begins with A; 'overlapping' lets them share that A, giving LIBRARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Record libraries are collections of sound recordings that people can borrow or consult.

clue.text: And this could be designated etc, before long

definitions.text: And this could be designated etc
definitions.meaning: etc stands for et cetera, which in plain English is the phrase 'and ...', so the two words after 'and' are meant

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a cryptic one: 'etc' is short for 'and so on', and the clue asks for the words after 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Etc' expands to 'and so on'; separately, the word means shortly or presently.

clue.text: Complete with yen to be a female

parts.note: to complete a form or a space is to fill it
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An instruction to fill in a form with a currency, as part of a sexing exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A filly is a young female horse.

clue.text: A psalm at start of Evensong in this part of church

parts.note: PS is the abbreviation for psalm, as in Bible references

indicators.note: at start of picks only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A psalm is sung at the start of evening service in this part of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded or vaulted recess, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Live surrounded by Lilian's damaging writings

indicators.note: surrounded by means the live word sits inside Lilian's name

parts.note: Lil is the short form of the name Lilian
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Lilian's household lives with a stream of slanderous letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' puts BE inside LIL, a short form of Lilian.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is defamation in published or written form.

clue.text: Dismay at day spent with mother's sister

parts.note: a mother's sister is an aunt

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed at a day spent with an aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt someone is to make them lose heart, to dismay them.

clue.text: Unthinking Eastern European and his reforms

parts.note: a Slav is a member of a people of eastern Europe such as Poles, Czechs or Russians

indicators.note: reforms signals that the letters of the little word his are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A thoughtless Eastern European man changes his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges HIS to ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A slavish copy or follower obeys without independent thought, so it is mindless.

clue.text: One produces a reaction about a chap

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a reaction concerning a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance added in chemistry to bring about a reaction.

clue.text: Had to secure pound (sovereign) for this old weapon

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word wraps round the pieces that follow

parts.note: taken as written
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight, from Latin libra
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the reigning monarch or sovereign

explanation.surface: A soldier pays a pound coin, a sovereign, for an antique weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' looks like the gold coin beside 'pound' but here it means the monarch, ER. 'to secure' puts LB and ER inside HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a medieval pole weapon combining a spear and a battle-axe.

clue.text: Wretched pal cruelly held by Nazi war criminal

indicators.note: held by means the scrambled friend word is placed inside the war criminal's name

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy, convicted at Nuremberg

indicators.note: cruelly signals that the letters of pal are treated harshly and mixed up

explanation.surface: A poor friend is cruelly held captive by a Nazi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruelly' rearranges PAL to APL, and 'held by' puts it inside HESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unlucky or unfortunate, a pitiable state.

clue.text: Turn away fed up with lecture

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lect. is a dictionary abbreviation for lecture

explanation.surface: Someone sick of being lectured looks away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like 'bored', but 'up' turns FED to DEF in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect is to divert something from its course.

clue.text: Ghost almost appearing in Macbeth and in Parisian feast

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the ghost's name is dropped

parts.note: Banquo is the murdered character whose ghost appears at the feast in Shakespeare's Macbeth
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A ghost turns up, as in Macbeth, at a Paris dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in Macbeth' tells you which ghost is meant; 'almost' cuts BANQUO to BANQU. Fittingly, Banquo's ghost appears at a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is a grand formal meal, a feast.

clue.text: Complaint over meal that's very nourishing

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the complaint above the meal

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
tea is an early evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A grumble about a meal that is very wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA is also the evening meal in much of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a broth made by stewing beef, traditionally given to invalids as a strengthening food.

clue.text: Nevertheless had to suppress friend's hunting cry

indicators.note: had to suppress means the first piece holds the second down inside it

parts.note: tho, short for though, means nevertheless
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Even so, someone had to keep a friend's hunting call quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had to suppress' puts ALLY inside THO.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the shout fox-hunters give when the fox is sighted.

clue.text: Expected a soldier

parts.note: par is the expected or normal standard, as in par for the course

explanation.surface: A soldier was expected to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'para' is short for paratrooper.
explanation.definitionFit: A para is a paratrooper, a soldier trained to drop by parachute.

clue.text: Singular dessert will come later

indicators.note: making a plural singular means removing its final S

parts.note: afters is an informal British word for pudding or dessert

explanation.surface: A single pudding will be served at the end of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for pudding; 'Singular' treats it as a plural and takes off its S.
explanation.definitionFit: The word as an adverb means subsequently or at a later time.

clue.text: Old friend is one to be valued?

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An old friend is someone to treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful one: a gemstone is something valued, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a precious gemstone, the sort of thing valued by a jeweller.

clue.text: Affectedly quaint women going in support of golfer

indicators.note: going in means the women letter is placed inside the golfer's support

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golfer rests the ball on

explanation.surface: Women take a supporting role for a golfer in a quaint way.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for cute or dainty in an overdone way.

clue.text: Thus having to go on foot is not brilliant

indicators.note: in a down clue, going on means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: so means thus or in this way

explanation.surface: Going about on foot is not a bright idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft light is muted, gentle rather than dazzling.

clue.text: Finish women off with time to plan method of saving

parts.note: an end is a finish

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of women are thrown out of their order

parts.note: a policy is a plan or course of action

explanation.surface: Someone means to finish off the women, given time to plot it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges WOMEN to OWMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment policy is a life insurance plan that pays out a lump sum, used as a long-term savings vehicle.

clue.text: Half of onlookers will hold us to be dodgy

indicators.note: will hold means the first piece wraps round the second
half of means only the first five of the ten letters of the onlookers word are kept

parts.note: spectators are people who watch, onlookers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Half the crowd will hold that we are a shady lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' cuts SPECTATORS to SPECT, and 'will hold' puts US inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspect as an adjective means questionable or not to be trusted.

clue.text: New trade company producing 30s designs

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of trade are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new trading company produces designs from the 1930s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TRADE to ARTDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative style that flourished in the 1920s and 1930s.
